sources.entry: CotEditor - Lightweight Plain-Text Editor for macOS.

summary.one_liner: CotEditor is a lightweight, macOS-native plain text editor written in Swift.
summary.what_it_does: CotEditor is a plain text editor for macOS built to follow macOS UI conventions and behaviors. It is described as a document-based Cocoa application that uses NSTextView and related text system APIs. The README says it aims to handle a wide range of plain text formats, with emphasis on encoding support and predictable editing. It is localized into many languages, including English, several Chinese variants, Japanese, Korean, German, French, and others. The README gives build instructions for local ad-hoc builds and for distribution builds, both done through Xcode. It also points to CONTRIBUTING.md for contribution guidelines.
use_cases: lightweight plain text editing on a Mac
editing notes and everyday text files
working with legacy or niche text formats and encodings
writing code or config files in a simple editor
running a locally built macOS text editor
how_to_run: Open Configurations/CodeSigning.xcconfig and uncomment #include "CodeSigning-AdHoc.xcconfig" for ad-hoc builds.
notable: Built as a macOS-native app that follows system UI conventions and document-based Cocoa architecture
Design philosophy favors simplicity and rejects features that deviate from standard macOS behavior
caveats: Only the latest two major macOS releases are supported; older systems must use an archived version
Built and developed with Xcode; no build instructions for other platforms
